evidence: Sources read: frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (openpyxl read_only, in memory) Quality Checks row 45 = #44 'dimension_and_criterion_weights_are_honest' and Internal Quality Checks row 45 annotation (Mukesh: functionality has 60 percent, and within functionality the verifier defines its own weightage; same for aesthetics); rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Delivery profile line 28: 'Reward is shaped - functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2'); references/quality-checks.md section 44 (sanity-check max contribution of non-functional dimensions), plus 42 and 43; references/staged-task-contract.md scoring.toml section ('Dimension weight lives here and nowhere else'); references/deterministic-checks.md (check-scoring-policy / check-rubric-schema recipes); qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md; frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/{scoring.toml,tools/score.py}; task instruction.md, environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py, all five judge.toml, scored/{functional,polish,visual}/prompt.md gate sections. DIMENSION LEVEL: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template (diff empty): [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0, [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2, [floors] functional=0.05; tests/tools/score.py identical to template. No judge.toml [judge] block carries a weight key (tomllib parse). Gates carry no reward mass. Functional 0.6 > polish 0.2 = visual 0.2, matching the profile. Polish here is not style: its five binary rows (scored/polish/judge.toml lines 17-60) are all behavioural promises from the brief (live board preserves open card/note/focus/scroll; live thread preserves draft/focus; earlier-page place kept; failed send kept and not double-sent; session resume and per-user draft isolation). So behaviour carries 0.8 of the mass and pure style (visual, 5 likert rows) at most 0.2. Visual and polish sit behind the same in-dimension backend gate (create job + candidate, read back from an independent Observer context; scored/visual/prompt.md lines 11-12 force Likert 1 = normalized 0 on failure), so a static mock earns no style mass. CRITERION LEVEL (re-derived by tomllib): functional 44 binary rows, total weight 59.5; polish 5 rows total 12.0; visual 5 likert rows x 1.2 = 6.0 (equal, appropriate for parallel craft facets). The highest functional weights (2.5) go to the brief's headline promises: hro_stale_refused (functional/judge.toml line 204-210; brief: 'when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who'), hro_live_board (line 294-300; 15 s propagation), hro_candidate_private (line 393-399; 'They must never see our internal notes...'). 2.0 goes to all-or-none bulk, undo restores, undo conflict, refused put-back with focus, earlier paging, unread counts, scrolled-up unread and drafts. The lowest (0.5) go to narrow or gate-overlapping rows: hro_job_open and hro_add_candidate (job creation and candidate add are already exercised by the global gate, so low weight avoids double credit), hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals (negative-only) and hro_candidate_linked. No functional row grades file layout, stack or source structure; no weight rewards structure over behaviour. Polish weights put the two concurrency-preservation rows (3 each) above session resume 2.5, earlier place 2 and failed send 1.5, tracking the brief's emphasis ('the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled'). MAX CONTRIBUTION SANITY CHECK: per-row reward share = dim_weight*w/total. Largest functional row 0.6*2.5/59.5 = 0.0252; each visual row 0.2*1.2/6 = 0.040; polish rows 0.025-0.050. A single style row therefore outweighs any single functional row. This is an arithmetic consequence of the template-fixed 0.6/0.2/0.2 split over a 44-row functional rubric, not a task-authored inversion; dimension-level functional mass is 3x visual. COUNTEREXAMPLE ATTEMPTS: (a) Plausible broken app: passes the gate (persisted job/candidate), passes only hro_job_open + hro_add_candidate + hro_add_email_rules + hro_restart (3.5/59.5 = 0.0588 > floor 0.05), fails everything else, but has excellent styling (all visual 5). Reward = 0.6*0.0588 + 0.2*1.0 = 0.235, versus 0.8 for a fully working app with all-1 visuals. Ranking is preserved and functionality dominates, but style is about 85% of that broken app's reward. This is template-fixed weight/floor policy (rows 42/43 territory) and the task may not alter scoring.toml, so it is recorded as a Note for the owner, not a row-44 defect. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app with plain but clear visuals (all likert 3 -> 0.5 normalized) loses 0.1, consistent with the brief's 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters'; no conforming behaviour is weighted to zero or outweighed inside functional by a cosmetic row. EVIDENCE GAP (reason for risk=true): qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r13/raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. Weight honesty is assessed statically from the shipped weights; whether the configured judge's actual scores let these weights discriminate as intended is unmeasured. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
